demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- Management expects the coffee and hospitality businesses to benefit from structural growth drivers including rising café culture, premiumisation, expanding organised food service and growing out-of-home coffee consumption in India.
- Management flags continued exposure to coffee price volatility, climate-related production risks, rising input/logistics costs and global supply chain disruptions as factors affecting the coffee business outlook.
- Management expects the hospitality business to benefit from continued growth in domestic tourism, business travel and MICE activity.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Demand for hospitality services is closely linked to economic growth, disposable incomes and consumer confidence; slowdowns or reduced discretionary spending may hit occupancy and revenue.
- The hospitality business depends on sustained domestic and international tourism; geopolitical tensions, public health emergencies, natural disasters or travel restrictions could hurt tourist arrivals and occupancy.
- Competition from domestic and international hotel chains, boutique hotels, serviced apartments and alternative accommodation platforms, plus continuous room-inventory addition and aggressive pricing, may pressure occupancy, ARRs and margins.
- Exposure to inflation in employee costs, F&B procurement, utilities, energy, maintenance and transportation that may not be fully passable to customers.
- Hospitality is service-intensive and depends on skilled personnel; shortages, rising wage costs and attrition can affect operational efficiency and service quality.
- Hospitality operations are subject to food safety, fire/life safety, environmental, labour, taxation, liquor-licensing and tourism regulations; changes or approval delays can raise compliance costs.
- Use of digital booking platforms, online payments and hotel management systems exposes the business to cybersecurity threats and data-privacy risks that could affect customer trust and continuity.
- Exposure to extreme weather events, water scarcity and changing environmental regulations that may disrupt operations and require added investment in resilience.
